method: Each case has four order-balanced pairs on one host. The Codex editing comparisons ran on a second 32-core AMD Genoa host after two matched stock/current control pairs. Wall-time change is 1.100.0-1 minus 1.99.0-34. Two-sided 95% intervals use the paired differences and Student t with three degrees of freedom. Ratios use paired log times. Intervals describe individual cases.
publication_text:
We repeated all 14 flagged cases with both released Ohm SDKs. Each comparison has four pairs, with both SDKs running on the same machine. The paired 95% intervals showed that 6 cases were slower and 1 case was faster. The 95% intervals for 7 cases span zero.

| Case | Ohm 1.99.0-34 | Ohm 1.100.0-1 | Mean change | 95% interval for change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Codex cold Clippy | 119.32 s | 146.42 s | +27.11 s | +10.64 to +43.57 s |
| Ruff developer workflow · edit-check-test-check | 21.59 s | 25.69 s | +4.10 s | -0.39 to +8.59 s |
| Codex developer workflow · edit-test | 25.52 s | 26.29 s | +0.78 s | -1.24 to +2.79 s |
| Codex developer workflow · edit-fmt-clippy-test | 32.66 s | 31.56 s | -1.10 s | -8.41 to +6.21 s |
| Ruff editing replay · Run final strict Clippy for both affected packages | 15.29 s | 17.22 s | +1.93 s | -0.26 to +4.11 s |
| uv editing replay · Run local-mock-index installation integration test | 38.04 s | 41.13 s | +3.09 s | +1.71 to +4.47 s |
| Codex editing replay · Total wall time | 258.13 s | 308.02 s | +49.89 s | +33.97 to +65.80 s |
| Codex editing replay · Check the edited TUI library | 46.86 s | 71.86 s | +25.00 s | +20.37 to +29.64 s |
| Codex editing replay · Recheck the exact custom-height regression after integrating the widget | 28.85 s | 26.93 s | -1.92 s | -3.83 to -0.02 s |
| Codex editing replay · Run the exact strict Clippy lint used during the original CI fix | 60.62 s | 88.09 s | +27.48 s | +20.52 to +34.43 s |
| Codex editing replay · Validate the entire TUI package once | 33.94 s | 33.21 s | -0.72 s | -12.31 to +10.86 s |
| Ruff historical replay · Run strict Clippy for the changed core and semantic crates | 19.67 s | 20.25 s | +0.58 s | -1.05 to +2.20 s |
| ty editing replay · Run all semantic package tests | 48.41 s | 51.99 s | +3.58 s | -0.39 to +7.55 s |
| ty editing replay · Run Clippy for all semantic targets and features | 26.13 s | 30.45 s | +4.33 s | +2.13 to +6.52 s |

Positive changes mean the new release took longer. The comparisons include the upstream Rust version change and Ohm changes.

The Codex editing comparisons reused the 32-core AMD Genoa machine that had finished the uv benchmarks. We first repeated the original two stock/current pairs there. Stock Rust and Ohm 1.100 averaged 485.10 and 322.81 seconds on the original host, and 493.43 and 311.12 on the second. The source tree, lockfile and selection of 3,439 final TUI tests matched on both. In the four direct Ohm pairs, the largest command-level increase was “Run the exact strict Clippy lint used during the original CI fix” at +27.48 seconds. The complete Codex replay took 49.89 seconds longer on average.

All eight cold Codex Clippy runs exited successfully. Three of the four 1.100 runs also printed a recursion-depth warning at `core/src/session/mod.rs:3113`, previously recorded during release qualification. Cargo counted five duplicate warnings in those runs and six in the other 1.100 run. The two Codex developer comparisons retained 16 runs. The host and command monitors discarded 6 additional attempts. We verified all 80 command logs and 16 CPU traces for the accepted runs.

The uv comparison uses the same import-level allowance for `clippy::disallowed_types` in both SDKs. Both ran the same strict Clippy commands. Both Ruff SDKs ran Clippy with `-D warnings`. The 1.99 commands omit one allowance for `clippy::needless_nonzero_get`, a lint introduced after that release.
